title: Open a wooden pencil case and release the pen
instruction: Open the wooden pencil case. Turn and hold the orange release knob with one arm while the other lifts out the pen. Hold the pen clear of the case.
context: Wooden presentation cases hold pens in fitted inserts. A spring-return rotary catch adds a continuous release step during retrieval. See the product and mechanism references in the README.
setup: A closed 192 × 78 mm wooden case is fixed in a bench fixture. A 146 × 16 mm blue pen rests in a felt-lined slot with 72 mm of central finger relief. The orange rotary knob turns two steel keeper tabs away from the barrel and springs back when released.
scoring: 0.5 for a stable lid opening of at least 95°. 1.0 for a stable grasp with the pen 30 mm above the rim for 0.75 s, after the pen cleared the keeper while the opposite arm held the knob at least 35° open. See the README for the contact and speed criteria.
reset_notes: Fixed seed 0 with zero object jitter. Reset the pen in both saddles, the lid closed and the release knob at its spring-rest position.
fidelity: Native PhysX solves a passive hinged lid, a spring-return cam and a freely moving rigid pen. The torsion spring is an angular drive, and the cam tabs and pen interact through collision. The base is held by a visible bench fixture.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (seed 0 for both)
